review: The hymn is the argument from the lesser to the greater: 1:1–4 is Matt 6:28–30 with Ps 147:9, 2:1–4 is Matt 10:29–31 with Ps 104:12, 3:1–4 is Isa 49:15 (הֲתִשְׁכַּח אִשָּׁה עוּלָהּ) nearly verbatim, and 4:1–4 is Matt 10:30 (וְשַׂעֲרוֹת רֹאשְׁכֶם כֻּלָּן נִמְנוּ).
The refrain is a question in every stanza and the payload keeps the interrogative and the exclamation mark, because the hymn is an argument and its force depends on the repeated unanswered question.

2:1 דְּרוֹר בַּיִת — the Arabic عُصْفُورُ دُورٍ is the house sparrow; the Hebrew uses דְּרוֹר, the bird of Ps 84:4 and Prov 26:2, with בַּיִת to hold the Arabic's species, since biblical Hebrew has no separate sparrow-word.
3:3 keeps the print's slightly awkward claim (the sons are the dearest of His creation) as a verbless clause, rather than smoothing it into a comparison the Arabic does not make.
